summary: Both the prompt and the subject held at their dispatched digests, and I verified the prompt against the digest supplied in the dispatch before trusting the subject digest it carries. Every attack axis fails. The predecessor ledger is the strongest artifact of its kind I have reviewed in this corpus: twelve rows across three turns, every digest verified against live bytes, and the three rows describing my own verdicts exact in verdict, counts and finding ids. The claim most capable of being false — that D-070's already-performed file-08 edit still leaves these three rows undisposed — is true in the edited bytes, which now read 'DR-006, DR-007, DR-009, DR-011 remain without SATISFIED or scoped owner-recorded disposition.' file 08 moved since the last cycle because that edit landed, and this entry re-measured it rather than carrying a stale pin.

The title reads '# D-069 / D-071 / D-072 — Select Route B for DR-006, DR-007, DR-009' and the Protocol line reads 'D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3. Not a fourth turn of CONTESTED D-051 / D-052 / D-053.' This is the third application of a pattern the register already carries — D-017 was parked and succeeded by 'D-025–D-031, a new cycle, not a fourth turn of this one', and D-067 was parked and succeeded by D-070.

The attack 'title/protocol/path misidentify the cycle' fails: title, Protocol line, file path, all three section headings and all three overturn codes name the new numbering consistently, with the only D-051/052/053 references being explicitly labelled predecessor history.
There is no numbering collision. D-069, D-071 and D-072 are absent from COORD, whose highest present number is D-070.

The attack 'predecessor ledger missing, stale, or incomplete' fails, and I tested every row rather than sampling. All twelve ledger digests match live bytes: the three turn subjects, the three turn prompts, and all six reviewer verdict files. The CONTESTED commit 11a4e6998b48b762d46e313a470431ff68236db8 resolves to 'D-051/D-052/D-053: CONTESTED after three turns'.

The three ledger rows describing my own verdicts are exact, which is the part of the ledger I can test absolutely because I wrote those files. Turn 1: OBJECT, 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX C2-D051-053-SF1, 3 notes. Turn 2: OBJECT, 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX C2-D051-053-T2-SF1, 3 notes. Turn 3: CONSENT, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 2 notes. Verdicts, counts and finding ids all match what those files record.

The ledger is also the thing both reviewers asked for. My D-051-053 turn-3 note recorded that reviewer-verdict recitals carried no digest to hash against, and the disposition table records Codex's ADV-D051-053-T2-01 as asking for 'hash-pinned predecessor subjects plus both reviewers' verdict paths/digests/counts'. The ledger supplies exactly that, so the improvement landed rather than being restated.

The characterisation of the contested outcome is faithful to the register. The subject says 'Decision merits passed on Claude's side. Process ledger ADV-D051-053-T3-01 did not pass on Codex's side.' COORD's CONTESTED entry records 'Claude 2 turn 3 CONSENT on all three entries' and 'Codex turn 3 OBJECTIONS, 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX ADV-D051-053-T3-01 (wants a three-turn ledger disposing the turn-2 Codex finding on the frozen subject's protocol line)', and it pins my turn-3 verdict at fb386ef5…, the same digest the ledger carries.

The subject states D-070 is ADOPTED at commit e40b3f190e68264a24ac5098b1cef300434d6709, which resolves to 'D-070: adopt file-08 MF-6 notes for preview owner recordings', that it 'is not this file', and that 'These entries do not adopt or overturn D-070.' The claim about D-070's condition-1 row is true in the performed edit, which I treated as the sharpest check because file 08 has changed since the last cycle. The subject states 'This cycle selects Route B for those three rows; it does not owner-record them', and each entry's final clause reads 'Writes no disposition. Marks nothing SATISFIED. Authorizes no blueprint.' Independently, D-070's performed edit gave preview-scope owner-recording cell notes to DR-002, DR-005 and DR-010 among others, and gave none to DR-006, DR-007 or DR-009 — so the register itself still shows those three unrecorded.

D-072 correctly carries none, because D-002 names no DR-009 rides.

The attack 'invents D9 codes or treats applied heads as SATISFIED' fails. D-071 states 'This entry invents no D9 code' and rejects inventing preview D9 codes in its alternatives. The phrase 'is not SATISFIED of this row' appears twice, once for EIR v12 under D-003 in D-069 and once for r1 v1.9 under D-005 in D-072, each preceded by the statement that application of a lineage head is not binding recipes or park closure.

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED' and 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' fail: 'Marks nothing SATISFIED' and 'Authorizes no blueprint' each appear three times, 'Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization' appears three times, and the header adds two new refusals this cycle — 'Does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/' and 'Does not edit file 08.'

Examined and cleared: DR-001 is omitted from all three exclusion lists, which is principled rather than an oversight — DR-001 is SATISFIED, so no route selection is meaningful for it, and the preamble states as much.

The scope statements around the cycle are accurate. The unadopted D-059-063 five-entry draft is disclaimed as 'not this cycle and is not adopted here'. The preamble's claim that DR-002/003/004/005/008 have selections and owner recordings names D-058, D-065, D-064, D-060 and D-061, and that DR-010 is owner-recorded at preview scope by D-068 — all six of which I verified as ADOPTED in their own cycles. consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The decision merits are the ones I already consented to at D-051-053 turn 3, and the diff confirms they are unchanged apart from numbering and tightened exclusions. What is new is the process apparatus, and it is genuinely good: a twelve-row hash-pinned ledger whose every digest I verified, including the three rows describing my own verdicts, which are exact. Two checks deserve naming because they could have gone the other way. file 08 moved since the last cycle — D-070's edit landed — and this entry re-measured it instead of carrying the stale pin, which matters because the row it relies on lives inside the changed bytes. And its claim that D-070 still leaves these three rows undisposed I verified in the edited register rather than in the authorization I had reviewed earlier: the performed edit says exactly that, and gave cell notes to DR-002, DR-005 and DR-010 while giving none to DR-006, DR-007 or DR-009.
